ops.d: List every sites in the subscription.
List the sites in a resource group.
List every serverfarms in the subscription.
List the serverfarms in a resource group.

features.t: Web Apps (create, list, get, delete, start/stop/restart)
App Service plans (create, list, get, delete)
x: Capacity/worker metrics are not simulated; SKU is stored but does not change quota enforcement.

features.t: Configuration (General settings: stack, platform, TLS, debugging, client certificates)
x: Settings are stored and returned to SDKs/az CLI; most (TLS version, FTP state, Always On, ...) are not enforced by a running workload.

features.t: Environment variables (App settings, Connection strings)
Deployment slots (create, list, delete, swap)
x: Swap exchanges config/app settings/connection strings only; no real traffic routing or warm-up.

features.t: Custom domains (hostname bindings)
x: No real DNS/TXT ownership verification or TLS binding; the hostname is accepted and attached to the site.

features.t: Locks (resource-scoped management locks)
x: A CanNotDelete/ReadOnly lock on the Web App really blocks delete/write requests on it (409 ScopeLocked), but enforcement is scoped to the exact locked resource — it does not cascade from a resource-group- or subscription-scoped lock the way real ARM would.

features.t: App Service logs (application logging level, HTTP logs quota/retention)
x: Settings round-trip; there is no running workload to actually emit application/HTTP logs.

features.t: Tags
Activity log
x: Records create/update/delete/start/stop/restart/swap operations on the Web App and its sub-resources (slots, custom domains, locks, configuration); filters (severity, timespan, resource group) and export/columns actions are not simulated.

features.t: Access control (IAM): role assignments and built-in role definitions over ARM
x: Role assignments and role definitions are real ARM resources (Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments, roleDefinitions). The Role assignments list is ENFORCED scoped to this Web App (plus its subscription/resource-group ancestors, matching real Azure's inherited-access view) instead of the whole subscription — the same engine the Cosmos DB account and VM blades use; Roles stays subscription-wide, which matches real Azure (built-in role definitions are listed tenant-wide too).

features.t: Deployment Center (CI/CD source, FTPS credentials)
x: Real ARM control plane plus real deployments through the shared CI seam (core/ci_core.py): sourcecontrols/web (repo URL, branch, manual/continuous integration, GitHub Actions with a generated workflow YAML; scmType maintained), deployments + log, publishing credentials and basic-auth policies. Local Git (scmType LocalGit): a push (POST .../localgit, a Vyomi extension of the Kudu git receiver; with the Gitea git host (offline, VYOMI_CI_GITEA=1) a real git clone URL and real `git push`) commits to the app's repo, builds, and records a Success/Failed deployment with the build log. GitHub source: the branch tarball is fetched (public, or private with the user's own personal access token entered in the Deployment Center; stored server-side, never shown) and built on the offline appliance; on Nano there is no outbound HTTP so a GitHub sync is a Failed deployment saying so (Local Git works on Nano). Azure Repos / Bitbucket / generic git cannot be fetched (no HTTP git client) and are recorded Failed with that reason. The build produces a content-addressed package artifact (Dockerfile validated; container image builds use BuildKit on the offline appliance only); the App Service runtime does not hot-swap to the deployed package, the GitHub Actions workflow is generated and, when a personal access token is supplied (properties.vyomiAccessToken; offline appliance only - Nano cannot reach GitHub), committed to the connected repository through the GitHub Contents API (without a token it is generated but not committed; the pipeline itself runs on GitHub), and OAuth account authorization is not performed (PAT only).

features.t: Monitoring (Alerts, Metrics, Logs, Advisor recommendations, Health check, Diagnostic settings, Log stream, Process explorer)
x: Diagnostic settings (Microsoft.Insights/diagnosticSettings) are real: create/list/delete round-trip through the same generic engine every other Azure resource's Diagnostic settings page uses, scoped to this Web App's resource id. Export to the Log Analytics workspace is not simulated (no log/metric pipeline writes land there).

features.t: Development Tools (Clone App, Console, Advanced Tools, App Service Editor, Extensions)
x: Console, Advanced Tools (Kudu), App Service Editor, Process explorer, Log stream and Extensions are real over the Kudu API served as an ARM extension (azure.appservices.webapp.kudu, .extensions); commands run in the simulator's bounded shell against the app's virtual /home, not in a real container. Clone App is not modelled.

features.t: API (API Management link, API definition, CORS)
x: CORS allowed origins / credentials are stored on siteConfig.cors and returned to SDKs/az CLI; Vyomi has no real HTTP layer in front of the app, so the rule is never actually enforced against a cross-origin request.

features.t: Authentication, Identity, Application Insights, Backups, Certificates, Networking, WebJobs, Service Connector
x: Identity: enabling a system-assigned managed identity mints a stable principalId/tenantId that can be the subject of a role assignment on Access control (IAM); user-assigned identities are real too (references to Microsoft.ManagedIdentity/userAssignedIdentities are resolved, unknown ones rejected).

features.t: Scale up/out, Change App Service plan, Quotas
x: Scale up changes the plan's SKU, Scale out changes siteConfig.numberOfWorkers, and Change App Service plan re-points serverFarmId at another existing plan in the same resource group and OS — all real, round-tripping ARM PATCHes.

features.t: Automation (Tasks, Export template)
x: Tasks are real Logic App workflows (Recurrence trigger plus Http-to-ARM actions, core/azure_tasks_core.py): scheduled runs call the simulator's own ARM and keep results in the run output; only Recurrence triggers and Http/Compose actions run, there is no e-mail or Teams connector, and Nano only fires schedules while the tab is open.

features.t: Microsoft Defender for Cloud (this web app's recommendations)
x: Shows the live Defender for Cloud recommendations for this resource from Vyomi's rule engine (see azure.defender.recommendations); Azure's full built-in recommendation catalogue is not reproduced.

features.t: Diagnose and solve problems, Events (preview)
x: Diagnose and solve problems is real: detectors (core/azure_diagnose_core.py) are computed from the resource's live configuration, child resources and recorded operations; there is no platform telemetry behind a simulator, so none reads invented metrics and there is no AI troubleshooter.

features.t: Default documents, Path mappings, Error pages, Health check, API definition, API Management link
x: The app host (core/azure_webhost_core.py, served at /azure-data/site/{app}/...) APPLIES the site configuration: default documents (in order), path mappings (virtualApplications serve their own physical directory of the app's file system), custom error pages (403/404/500), HTTPS only (301), minimum TLS version (from the declared x-vyomi-tls-version header; no real TLS terminates), client certificate required, IP access restrictions, stopped app, health check probe (reported in x-vyomi-health), Always On (cold start on the first request after 20 idle minutes), and app settings are the environment (os.environ) of Python Function code. A Web App serves static content from its file system; handler mappings are stored but not executed (reported in x-vyomi-skipped) and no language runtime runs server-side Web App code.

features.t: WebJobs (triggered and continuous)
x: Triggered Python scripts really execute in a restricted sandbox (no filesystem, network or subprocess); other runtimes are refused at run time.

features.t: Service Connector
x: Creating a connection validates the target in this subscription and writes the real connection app settings (endpoint, plus a generated secret for secret auth); there is no network path, firewall rule or role assignment created for the target.

features.t: Quotas
x: File system storage limit is the published figure per plan tier; usage counts only the content Vyomi stores for the app (function code, WebJob scripts). CPU, memory and bandwidth quotas are not reported.

features.t: Authentication (App Service authentication)
x: authsettingsV2 is validated and round-trips (Entra registration, audiences, excluded paths); the function-app front door enforces unauthenticatedClientAction (302/401/403/AllowAnonymous) against the simulator token or a JWT whose claims validate. JWT signatures are not verified and there is no interactive sign-in or non-Entra provider. Web (non-function) app requests are not served, so nothing is enforced for them.

features.t: Autoscale
x: Autoscale settings targeting an App Service plan are evaluated (core/azure_autoscale_core.py) against the REAL request series the app host records (Requests, Http2xx/4xx/5xx, AverageResponseTime per site; CpuPercentage/MemoryPercentage are a load gauge = requests per second per instance against a nominal 20 rps, not measured CPU): scale-out if any rule triggers, scale-in only if all do, ChangeCount/PercentChangeCount/ExactCount, profile min/max clamp, cooldown, fixedDate profiles. The plan's instance count (sku.capacity) really changes and every action is recorded in the Run history (GET autoscaleSettings/{n}/vyomiHistory) and the Activity log. recurrence profiles, predictive autoscale and metrics other than those above are not evaluated; no instances are started (the app host is one in-process worker).

features.t: Certificates
x: Uploaded PFX files are stored with a SHA-1 thumbprint of the file; Vyomi does not parse the certificate, so subject, issuer and expiry are not read from it.

features.t: Clone App
x: Copies the site configuration, app settings and connection strings into a new app; there is no site content to copy and slots, backups and custom domains are not cloned.

features.t: Networking: regional VNet integration, access restrictions, hybrid connections
x: Inbound access restrictions are ENFORCED on requests to a Function App site (offline: /azure-data/functions/{app}/{fn}): rules evaluated by ascending priority, first match wins, implicit Deny all once an Allow rule exists, vnet-subnet / service-tag / Front Door x-azure-fdid header rules matched against the caller identity declared with x-vyomi-source-ip / x-vyomi-source-subnet / x-vyomi-source-service-tag headers (an undeclared caller is an unknown public client). 403 Forbidden otherwise. Nano has no site front end, so there it is validated config only; web apps (non-function) have no served runtime in Vyomi to enforce against.

features.t: Application Insights (component, requests, failures, dependencies, events)
x: A real Microsoft.Insights/components resource linked through the app's connection string; requests / failures / dependencies / events / traces are read from the OTLP-ingested trace + log store (and requests Vyomi measured for the app). No Kusto query engine, Live Metrics stream or Application Map.

features.t: Tasks (Logic App-backed task templates)
x: A task is a REAL Microsoft.Logic/workflows record (Recurrence trigger + Http actions against management.azure.com) created from a template via POST .../Microsoft.Logic/vyomiCreateTask; runs are fired by the simulator scheduler (core/schedule_core.py) or 'Run now' and call the simulator's own ARM, so the effect is real (power state, restarts, key rotation, usage snapshots), with per-action results in Microsoft.Logic/workflows/runs. Only Recurrence triggers and Http-to-ARM/Compose actions run (anything else fails the run with ActionNotSupported); the managed identity is not authorised (RBAC is not evaluated); workflow expressions are not evaluated; there are no e-mail/Teams connectors, so report tasks keep their result in the run output. Missed schedules coalesce into one run; Nano only fires schedules while the tab is open.

features.t: Advanced Tools (Kudu): environment, settings, deployments, tool links
x: Served as an ARM extension under sites/{site}/kudu/api (vfs, command, processes, deployments, settings, environment, logstream, siteextensions), not as a separate https://{site}.scm.azurewebsites.net host, so the real Kudu dashboard UI and its Git/zip-deploy endpoints are not served there (use Deployment Center / the Local Git extension).

features.t: Console (Kudu command console over the site's files and app settings)
x: There is no operating-system process behind the simulated site, so programs cannot be executed; the interpreter covers file, environment and process-listing commands only.

features.t: App Service Editor (edit the site's deployed files)
x: Edits the site's virtual file system (Deployment Center package contents, function sources, hostingstart.html, log files). Edits layer on top of deployed content and persist; the simulated runtime does not hot-swap to edited files. No syntax highlighting, no Git or debugging integration.

features.t: Process explorer (processes of the site's runtime)
x: The process table is MODELLED from the site's real state (runtime worker per instance, the Kudu/scm process, running continuous WebJobs); CPU time is the sum of the real measured invocation durations. It is not an operating-system process table: no kill/dump/profile actions and no per-thread detail.

features.t: Log stream (live tail of the site's logs)
x: Tails real recorded lines (function invocations, WebJob runs, deployments, lifecycle and console actions) by polling a cursor every 2 seconds; stdout of a long-running workload does not exist because the simulated site runs no always-on process. Application logging level is reported but does not filter lines.

features.t: Extensions (site extension gallery and install state)
x: Windows apps only (Linux apps return 400, as in Azure). The gallery is a bundled list of well-known extensions; install/uninstall records state and a marker file under /home/SiteExtensions — the extension's own code is not downloaded or executed.

features.t: Secure unique default hostname (autoGeneratedDomainNameLabelScope)
x: The generated hostname is {name}-{hash}.{region}-01.azurewebsites.net with the hash derived from the chosen reuse scope (Tenant/Subscription/ResourceGroup/NoReuse); re-creating the app in scope reuses it, a live one is a 409, names over 40 characters are rejected. Without the setting the plain name is a global namespace (a second app with that name conflicts). The hostname is not resolvable by public DNS.

features.t: Create Web App > Database (linked database + connection string)
x: The wizard creates a real Azure SQL server + database (with the Azure-services firewall rule) or a Cosmos DB for NoSQL account through ARM and writes the connection string to the app's Connection strings and app settings. PostgreSQL, MySQL and Redis options of the real wizard are not offered; the database is created after the app, not in one deployment, so a failure part-way leaves the app created without the database.

features.t: Events (preview): Event Grid system events of the web app and its plan
x: Event subscriptions are real Microsoft.EventGrid/eventSubscriptions scoped to the site. Real events are raised by actual operations: Microsoft.Web.AppUpdated (site/config/app-settings writes and start/stop/restart), SlotSwapCompleted, BackupOperationCompleted and, on the plan, AppServicePlanUpdated. The Started/Failed/Preview variants (BackupOperationStarted/Failed, Restore*, SlotSwapStarted/Failed/WithPreview*) are accepted as filters but only fire from 'Send test event'. Delivery is real only to Service Bus queue/topic destinations on the offline appliance; other destinations (and every destination on Nano) are unreachable and resolve to dead-lettered/dropped.
